content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

I've drafted the baseline specification. No code yet — this is the first SDD gate, and I need your review before we plan.

## 📋 Specification ready for review

**Location:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`

### What the spec proposes — a bookmark app in four slices

| Priority | User story | What it delivers |
|----------|-----------|------------------|
| **P1** | Save a bookmark | Paste a web address, optionally a title; it's validated and stored |
| **P1** | Browse & open | See all saved bookmarks (newest first), click to open the original page |
| **P2** | Edit & delete | Rename titles, remove entries (with a confirmation) |
| **P3** | Find quickly | Filter the list by typing part of a title or address |

The first two (P1) together are the minimum viable product: a place to stash links and get them back.

### Key scope decisions (assumptions I made — please confirm)

These are the choices most likely to matter to you. I picked sensible defaults rather than blocking with questions, but they're worth a look:

- **Single user, single device, stored locally** — no accounts, sign-in, or cross-device sync in v1
- **Flat list + search** — no folders or tags in v1
- **Web pages only** (http/https)
- **Auto-fetching a page's real title** is best-effort; if it can't, the app shows a title derived from the address
- **Duplicate addresses** are prevented/flagged

### Also defined in the spec

- 12 functional requirements (FR-001–FR-012)
- 5 measurable success criteria (e.g. save a bookmark in under 15s; find one among 100 in under 10s)
- Edge cases (duplicates, missing titles, very long URLs, reload persistence)

---

**This gate is the point of SDD — please review the spec.** A few things worth your explicit call:

1. Are the **scope boundaries** right, or do you want folders/tags, accounts, or multi-device sync in v1?
2. Is **local, single-user storage** acceptable, or should bookmarks live on a server?
3. Any user story you'd **reprioritize, drop, or add**?

Once you approve (or tell me what to change), I'll move to **speckit-plan**. If anything's ambiguous, I can also run a structured clarify pass first. Nothing gets built until spec and plan are approved.

Local, single-user storage is fine for the first version; I don’t need accounts or syncing yet.

I do want tags in v1, though. A flat list will become difficult to manage, so I should be able to add multiple tags, reuse existing ones, and filter by a tag. Search should also be part of the core release and ignore capitalization.

Please also move editing and deleting into the core release. Editing should cover the address and description as well as the title. When I save an address that already exists, take me to the existing bookmark so I can update it instead of merely showing an error. Automatically collecting the page title, description, and icon would also make saving much more useful.

Please revise the specification around those points before planning.

Spec revised. Here's what changed based on your feedback — still at the spec gate, no code yet.

## 📋 Revised specification — `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`

### Core release (v1) now includes everything you asked for

| Priority | User story | Change |
|----------|-----------|--------|
| **P1** | Save with **auto-collected** title, description & icon | ⭐ new — app fetches page details automatically, falls back to address-derived title if unavailable |
| **P1** | Browse & open | list now shows description, icon, and tags |
| **P1** | **Tags** | ⭐ promoted into v1 — add multiple tags, reuse existing ones (no duplicates), filter by a tag |
| **P1** | **Search** | ⭐ promoted into core — matches title/description/address/tags, **ignores capitalization** |
| **P1** | **Edit & delete** | ⭐ promoted into core — editing covers **address, title, and description**; delete requires confirmation |
| **P2** | Save existing address → **open it for update** | ⭐ new — re-saving a known address takes you to the existing bookmark to edit, not just an error |

### Specific points you raised, and how they're captured

- **Editing covers address + description + title** → FR-012 (edited address is re-validated).
- **Duplicate address opens the existing bookmark to update** → FR-014, plus FR-015 treats addresses differing only by case or trailing slash as the same. SC-006 makes it measurable (100% of the time, no duplicate created).
- **Search ignores capitalization** → FR-011 + acceptance scenario ("NEWS" matches "news").
- **Tags: multiple, reusable, filterable** → FR-009/FR-010, User Story 3.
- **Auto-collect title/description/icon** → FR-003; FR-004 guarantees saving still succeeds if collection fails, and SC-001 says you don't wait on it.

### Unchanged scope (per your confirmation)

- Local, single-user, single-device storage — no accounts or sync in v1.

### One small design note in the spec (not blocking)

Tags are treated as **free-form labels you type/reuse inline** — there's no separate tag-management screen in v1 beyond reuse and filtering. Flag it if you'd rather have a dedicated tag manager.

---

**Please review the revised spec at this gate.** If it reflects what you want, say the word and I'll proceed to **speckit-plan** (the implementation plan) for your review. If anything's still off, I'll revise the spec again first.

This revised specification reflects what I want. Free-form tags with reuse and filtering are sufficient; I don’t need a separate tag-management screen in v1. Please proceed to the implementation plan.

The plan and design artifacts are ready. This is the **plan gate** — please review before I generate the task breakdown. No application code has been written.

## 🛠️ Implementation Plan — `specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md`

### Proposed technical approach

The one decision that shapes everything: **auto-collecting a page's title, description, and icon (FR-003) requires fetching the remote page** — a browser can't do that (cross-origin restrictions). So the app needs a small backend, which also satisfies your runtime environment (server on port 4000).

| Aspect | Choice | Why |
|--------|--------|-----|
| **Runtime** | Node.js 24 + Express, single process | Provided by the image; `npm start` serves both UI and API on port 4000 |
| **Storage** | Local SQLite file | Local, single-user persistence; handles the bookmark↔tag many-to-many and case-insensitive search cleanly |
| **Metadata** | Server fetches page, parses `<head>` for title/description/icon | Best-effort; **save never blocks or fails** if collection is slow or the site is dead (FR-004, SC-001) |
| **Frontend** | Plain HTML/CSS/vanilla JS, no build step | UI is small (list, add/edit form, search, tag filter) |
| **Testing** | `node --test` for API + logic; Playwright 1.61.0 (pinned) for one end-to-end flow | Matches the installed browser version |

### Design artifacts generated (all in `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`)

- **research.md** — 8 decisions with rationale + rejected alternatives (why a backend, why SQLite, non-blocking save, address normalization, etc.)
- **data-model.md** — three tables: `Bookmark` (address, normalized key for dedupe, title, description, icon, timestamps), `Tag` (case-insensitive unique name), `bookmark_tags` (many-to-many)
- **contracts/api.md** — ~7 REST endpoints. Notably `POST /api/bookmarks` returns the **existing** bookmark (not just an error) when the address is already saved (FR-014/SC-006)
- **quickstart.md** — setup + 10 manual validation scenarios mapped to your user stories

### Notable design points worth your eye

- **Duplicate detection** normalizes case + trailing slash, so `Example.com/` = `example.com` (FR-015), and re-saving opens the existing entry to edit.
- **Non-blocking save**: the bookmark saves instantly with an address-derived title, then details fill in when the fetch completes.
- **No constitution gates**: the project constitution is an unfilled template, so there are no principles to check against — noted in the plan.

---

**Please review the plan.** If the tech approach (Node + SQLite + small backend for metadata) and the design look right, approve and I'll run **speckit-tasks** to produce the dependency-ordered task breakdown for your review. If you'd prefer different technology or a different approach to any decision, tell me and I'll revise the plan first.
The plan looks good to me. Saving immediately and filling in page details afterward is the behavior I want, and local storage remains appropriate. Please proceed with the task breakdown.

## ✅ Task Breakdown — `specs/001-bookmark-manager/tasks.md`

**51 tasks**, organized by user story so each is an independently testable increment.

| Phase | Tasks | What it delivers |
|-------|-------|------------------|
| **1. Setup** | T001–T005 (5) | Node project, pinned deps (incl. Playwright 1.61.0), directory skeleton |
| **2. Foundational** | T006–T010 (5) | SQLite schema (3 tables), Express bootstrap on `0.0.0.0:4000`, address normalization, UI shell |
| **3. US1 — Save + auto-collect** 🎯 | T011–T018 (8) | Save a bookmark; metadata fetched best-effort, non-blocking |
| **4. US2 — Browse & open** | T019–T023 (5) | Newest-first list, open in new tab, empty state |
| **5. US3 — Tags** | T024–T032 (9) | Multiple reusable tags, tag filter |
| **6. US4 — Search** | T033–T036 (4) | Case-insensitive search across title/description/address/tags |
| **7. US5 — Edit & delete** | T037–T043 (7) | Edit address/title/description, delete with confirmation |
| **8. US6 — Re-save opens existing** | T044–T047 (4) | Duplicate address → open existing to update |
| **9. Polish** | T048–T051 (4) | End-to-end Playwright flow, `app.json`, quickstart validation |

### Key characteristics

- **Suggested MVP**: US1 + US2 (both P1) — save with auto-details, then browse/open. Usable on its own.
- **Tests included** (the plan called for them): unit tests for normalization + metadata parsing, contract tests per endpoint, one Playwright end-to-end flow.
- **Every task has a task ID, file path, and — for story tasks — a story label.** `[P]` marks tasks on separate files that can run in parallel.
- **Traceability**: tasks cite the FRs and success criteria they satisfy (e.g. T044/T045 → FR-014/SC-006; T033 → FR-011).

### Note on ordering

The P1 stories (US1–US5) share `src/bookmarks.js` and `src/server.js`, so they're sequenced rather than fully parallel; `[P]`-marked test and static-file tasks still parallelize within each phase.

---

**This is the final gate before code.** If the task breakdown looks right, approve and I'll run **speckit-implement** to build the app against these tasks — after which I'll make it available for you to review at `http://maker:4000`. If you'd like to reorder, add, or cut any tasks, tell me and I'll revise `tasks.md` first.

Optionally, I can also run **speckit-analyze** first (a non-destructive consistency check across spec/plan/tasks) before implementing — just say the word.

## ✅ Bookmark Manager — implemented and running

All six approved user stories are built, tested, and live for your review.

### Available now for review

**Open `http://maker:4000`** — the app is running with a clean empty state, ready for you to add your first bookmark.

### What's implemented (all approved stories)

| Story | Status |
|-------|--------|
| **US1** Save with auto-collected title/description/icon (non-blocking) | ✅ verified — saving `example.com` filled in "Example Domain" automatically |
| **US2** Browse newest-first, open in new tab, empty state | ✅ |
| **US3** Multiple reusable tags + tag filter | ✅ |
| **US4** Case-insensitive search across title/description/address/tags | ✅ |
| **US5** Edit address/title/description; delete with confirmation | ✅ |
| **US6** Re-saving a known address opens the existing bookmark to update | ✅ |

### Verification

- **19/19** unit + API contract tests pass (`npm test`)
- **1/1** Playwright end-to-end flow passes (save → tag → filter → search → edit → delete → dedupe)
- Live smoke test confirmed auto-enrichment and the clean empty state

### How it was built (per the approved plan)

- Node.js 24 + Express, single process on `0.0.0.0:4000`
- Local SQLite (`data/bookmarks.db`) — three tables per the data model
- Server-side metadata fetch (avoids browser CORS), non-blocking so saves return instantly
- Plain HTML/CSS/JS frontend, no build step

### Two issues found and fixed during implementation (both routed correctly)

- A **test race** (test typed before the edit form finished loading) — fixed the test, spec unchanged.
- A genuine **app bug**: in the duplicate-save path, `beginEdit` was clearing the "already bookmarked" notice right after it was set — fixed by reordering in `app.js`. This was a fidelity fix against the approved spec (US6), so no spec/plan change was needed.
